text: Cattle housing (កន្លែងចិញ្ចឹមគោ) should provide space to stand/lie, clean water, feeding areas, shade, safe footing, drainage, and ventilation -- it doesn't need to be an expensive building; a simple roofed shelter with good airflow is often more practical than an enclosed one. During the wet season, prioritize drainage and a dry resting area since mud and standing water increase contamination around feed/water points. During the dry season, prioritize shade, airflow, and reliable clean water for heat management. Biosecurity (ជីវសុវត្ថិភាព) means reducing disease entry: obtain cattle from sources with known health history, avoid visibly sick animals, and keep newly purchased or returning cattle separate from the herd for an observation period set by veterinary guidance (not a fixed universal number) before mixing. Shared grazing, communal water, livestock markets, transport, visitors, and shared equipment can all spread disease -- these risks can be reduced, not eliminated, for smallholders using communal resources. Clean obviously contaminated equipment before reuse between animals/farms. If an animal shows fever, severe coughing, nasal discharge, diarrhea, unexplained weight loss, mouth/foot lesions, sudden weakness, unusual abortions, or sudden death, separate it where practical and get veterinary advice -- isolation alone does not treat disease. Do not assume a specific cattle breed dominates Preah Vihear; record the farmer's actual type (local/native, improved, crossbred, unknown).
